'''X-wing starfighters''', also known as the '''X-wing class''', were a type of [[starfighter]] marked by their distinctive [[S-foils]] that resembled the [[High Galactic]] script's character "X" in attack formation. They were heavily armed with four laser cannons on the S-foils and [[proton torpedo launcher]]s in the fuselage. X-wings were designed for dogfighting and long missions. During the [[Galactic Civil War]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] used X-wing models like the [[T-65B X-wing starfighter]] and [[T-65C-A2 X-wing starfighter|T-65C-A2 X-wing]] in many battles, deploying X-wings in engagements such as the [[Attack on Lothal]], the [[Battle of Yavin]], the [[Battle of Endor]], and the [[Battle of Jakku]].

Approximately thirty [[Standard year|years]] later, a different and upgraded variation of X-wing, the [[T-70 X-wing starfighter|T-70]], was used by the [[Resistance]], whereas a more advanced model, the [[T-85 X-wing starfighter|T-85]], was used by the [[New Republic Defense Fleet]].

==History==
===Design and development===
The X-wing was descended from [[Incom Corporation]]'s [[Clone Wars]]–era [[Starfighter|Fighter]], namely the [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter]], [[Clone Z-95 starfighter|Clone Z-95 Headhunter]], and [[Z-95 Headhunter]]. Incom's engineers strove to build a well-rounded, [[hyperdrive]]-equipped [[Snub-fighter|snubfighter]] with no exploitable weakness. The new starfighter was intended to become the backbone of the [[Imperial Navy]], but political forces led to the [[Galactic Empire]] deciding to rely on [[Sienar Fleet Systems]]' more affordable [[TIE series|TIE fighter series]]. The Alliance to Restore the Republic then adopted the X-wing design as its own.<ref name="Ultimate Visual Guide" />

In [[5 ABY]], [[Incom-FreiTek Corporation]] introduced the T-70 model, which incorporated many improvements over the T-65 series. The Incom engineers, having learned a valuable lesson from the loss of so many X-wings in the trenches at [[Battle of Yavin]], equipped the T-70 with a swiveling [[blaster cannon]] that could be used to fend off attacks from behind. At least one prototype had been constructed prior to the [[Battle of Jakku]].<ref name="Empire's End">''[[Aftermath: Empire's End]]''</ref> By 34 ABY, the New Republic had retired most of its T-70s in favor of the T-85s, which were even more capable than the already impressive T-70s.<ref name="Before the Awakening" />

===Operational history===
====Galactic Civil War====
=====Early battles=====
[[File:Attack_on_Lothal.png|thumb|right|300px|Assorted Rebel Fighter exit hyperspace for an attack on Lothal.]]
The [[T-65B X-wing starfighter|T-65B]] model was in use<ref name="N5">{{Andor|Narkina 5 (episode)}}</ref> as early as [[5 BBY]].<ref name="Andor 8 Date">"Narkina 5" begins a [[Standard month|month]] after "[[Kassa (episode)|Kassa]]," which dates itself to [[5 BBY]].</ref> [[Saw Gerrera]]'s [[Partisans]] had several of them in their livery during that period.<ref name="N5" /> Gerrera was among the first rebel leaders to see how useful the T-65 would be in rebel operations and had stolen eight via a violent [[raid on an Incom warehouse]]. Dubbed the [[Cavern Angels]] for the Partisans' habit of hiding material in caves, these X-wings were used as early as the Partisans' stay on [[Segra Milo]].<ref name="DawnRebellion">''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]''</ref>

The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] recovered information about the X-wing via the [[rescue of Incom personnel]]<ref name="RRaRS">{{EncyclopediaCite|Republic, Rebel, and Resistance Starfighters}}</ref> and operated T-65B X-wings as early as [[1 BBY]]. During the [[attack on Lothal]], at least ten [[T-65B X-wing starfighter|T-65B X-wing Fighter]] alongside [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber]]s participated in the assault, but all were destroyed by the Imperial defenses. [[Hera Syndulla]], [[Mart Mattin]], [[Secon Daree]], [[C1-10P]], and [[R3-A3]] survived being shot down, but many other pilots were killed and their astromechs destroyed.<ref name="Rebel Assault">{{Rebels|Rebel Assault}}</ref>

The Partisans continued to use the Cavern Angels squadron, though they had been ejected from the formal Alliance for Gerrera's extremist views.<ref name="Ultimate Visual Guide" /> Rebel X-wings saw action shortly before the outbreak of the [[Galactic Civil War]] in both the [[Liberation of Erso]]<ref name="SWBF">''[[Star Wars Battlefront]]''</ref> and the [[Mission to Eadu]].<ref name="RO">''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref>

=====Open war begins=====
[[File:XwingDiveAtShieldGate-CineFex151.png|thumb|left|300px|A T-65 X-wing piloted by [[Antoc Merrick]] attacks the Scarif Shield Gate.]]
The full-scale Galactic Civil War began with the [[Battle of Scarif]], a costly but significant victory for the Alliance. The newly assembled squad, [[Rogue One]], a special forces team created by [[Jyn Erso]], [[Cassian Jeron Andor|Cassian Andor]], [[Baze Malbus]], [[Chirrut Îmwe]], [[Bodhi Rook]], and [[K-2SO]] disobeyed direct orders from [[Alliance High Command]] and instead deployed itself to [[Scarif]] in a desperate bid to steal the technical readouts for the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[battle station]], and was subsequently joined by the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]]. X-wings from [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]], [[Green Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Green Squadron]], [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Blue Squadron]], and [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]] engaged Imperial TIEs and attempted to destroy the Shield Gate, while the [[capital ship]]s joined the Shield Gate assault and fought the Imperial [[Star Destroyer]]s. Shortly after the Alliance acquired the [[Death Star plans]], the Death Star arrived at Scarif and fired a low-power blast at the [[Citadel Tower]], killing all forces at the Imperial surface installation.<ref name="RO" />

[[File:Yavin_dogfight.png|thumb|right|300px|X-wings and TIEs engage in ship-to-ship combat above the surface of the Death Star]]
Within days of Scarif, the Empire learned that the Alliance was headquartered at [[Yavin 4]], and deployed the Death Star to crush the Alliance. The Alliance, having learned of the battle station's fatal design flaw, deployed a force of 30 Starfighters (including 22 X-wings) to attempt a series of attack runs on the [[planet]]-killing [[space station]]. The result was another costly victory for the Alliance. [[Luke Skywalker]], a legendary [[Force-sensitive]] [[Rebel pilot]], famously fired a pair of [[proton torpedo]]es into the Death Star's [[thermal exhaust port]], causing a chain reaction in the [[reactor]] that destroyed the entire station. The Death Star was gone but the Alliance lost 27 Starfighters (including 20 X-wings) in the assault.<ref name="ANH" />

Sometime during [[0 ABY]], three X-wings of [[Red Squadron]] were deployed in a [[mission to Giju]], which resulted in the rescue of multiple Alliance agents.<ref name="Weapon of a Jedi">''[[The Weapon of a Jedi: A Luke Skywalker Adventure]]''</ref>

A few days after the [[Battle of Yavin]], [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] and [[Evaan Verlaine]] disobeyed orders from Alliance High Command and departed on [[mission to rescue the survivors of Alderaan]]. Skywalker and [[Wedge Antilles]] were scrambled to intercept their shuttle, but the rebels jumped to hyperspace.<ref name="Leia 1">[[Princess Leia 1|''Princess Leia'' 1]]</ref>

After the [[Assault on Cymoon]], Luke Skywalker and R2-D2 flew an X-wing to [[Hradreek]] in order to obtain [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] for the Rebel war effort. Before long, a four-sided [[Skirmish on Hradreek|skirmish]] erupted over possession of [[Darth Atrius' lightsabers]], with R2 rescuing Skywalker by bringing him the ship.<ref name="Star Wars Annual 4">[[Star Wars Annual (2015) 4|''Star Wars Annual'' (2015) 4]]</ref>

Later, Skywalker flew an X-wing from the Alliance Fleet to Tatooine, accompanied by R2-D2. There, he revisited [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]]'s hut and discovered the deceased Jedi Master's journal. Disappointed that the journal didn't contain any information on Jedi training, Skywalker set course for [[Nar Shaddaa]].<ref name="Star Wars 4">[[Star Wars (2015) 4|''Star Wars'' (2015) 4]]</ref><ref name="Star Wars 5">[[Star Wars (2015) 5|''Star Wars'' (2015) 5]]</ref><ref name="Star Wars 6">[[Star Wars (2015) 6|''Star Wars'' (2015) 6]]</ref><ref name="Star Wars 7">[[Star Wars (2015) 7|''Star Wars'' (2015) 7]]</ref><ref name="Star Wars 8">[[Star Wars (2015) 8|''Star Wars'' (2015) 8]]</ref>

X-wings would again see large-scale action against the Empire in the [[Battle of Vrogas Vas]]. The battle was a costly defeat for the Alliance, with Blue Squadron completely destroyed and Red Squadron suffering heavy casualties.<ref name="Vader Down 1">[[Vader Down 1|''Vader Down'' 1]]</ref>

=====Battles continue=====
[[File:Darkink-ANewHope.png|thumb|left|250px|A rebel pilot and their astromech droid engages TIE fighters within an X-wing.]]
X-wings were also deployed to [[Sunspot Prison]] in the [[Prison siege at Sunspot|aftermath]] of [[Eneb Ray]]'s assault.<ref name="Star Wars 19">[[Star Wars (2015) 19|''Star Wars'' (2015) 19]]</ref>

The Alliance struck back against the Empire with the [[Hijacking of the Harbinger|hijacking of the ''Harbinger'']], a major space battle that resulted a rare case of an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] being successfully boarded and hijacked.<ref name="SW22">[[Star Wars (2015) 22|''Star Wars'' (2015) 22]]</ref> The Alliance used the [[Harbinger (Imperial I-class)|''Harbinger'']] to break through the [[Siege on Tureen VII]] and bring relief supplies to the planet's population. Although the hijacking ended with an Alliance victory, it resulted in [[C-3PO]]'s capture by [[Task Force 99]].<ref name="SW 25">[[Star Wars (2015) 25|''Star Wars'' (2015) 25]]</ref> The [[astromech droid]] [[R2-D2]] took it upon himself to stage a [[mission to rescue C-3PO]] in a stolen X-wing,<ref name="Star Wars 26">[[Star Wars (2015) 26|''Star Wars'' (2015) 26]]</ref> while Luke Skywalker and [[Essfour|S4]] gave chase and embarked on a [[Mission to Vagadarr Prime (Luke Skywalker)|mission to Vagadarr Prime]].<ref name="Star Wars 29">[[Star Wars (2015) 29|''Star Wars'' (2015) 29]]</ref>

Later, General [[Davits Draven]] deployed X-wings to raid [[Grakkus Jahibakti Tingi]]'s safe house on [[Teth]].<ref name="Star Wars 35">[[Star Wars (2015) 35|''Star Wars'' (2015) 35]]</ref>

At least five Rebel X-wings saw action in a [[dogfight over Odona]], where a pair of them shot down a TIE fighter. They were deployed Odona again to help rescue Han Solo and Leia Organa when a [[Mission to Odona|mission]] to scout locations for a new Rebel base devolved into a skirmish with [[Frax]] and [[Selt]].<ref name="Annual 3">[[Star Wars Annual (2015) 3|''Star Wars Annual'' (2015) 3]]</ref>

X-wings also defended from Imperial forces that launched an [[attack on the Rebel fleet]] shortly before the [[mission to Crait]].<ref name="Storms of Crait">[[The Last Jedi – The Storms of Crait 1|''The Last Jedi – The Storms of Crait'' 1]]</ref>

X-wings again saw large-scale action at the [[mutiny on Mon Cala]], a strategic Alliance victory. After the battle, the [[Mon Cala Mercantile Fleet]] became part of the Alliance Fleet, but the [[Mon Calamari]] [[King]] [[Lee-Char]] and his [[Regent]] [[Dors Urtya]] were both killed by Imperial forces.<ref name="Star Wars 48">[[Star Wars (2015) 48|''Star Wars'' (2015) 48]]</ref><ref name="Star Wars 49">[[Star Wars (2015) 49|''Star Wars'' (2015) 49]]</ref>

[[File:ApproachingTheCruiser-2015StarWars53.jpg|thumb|right|300px|X-wings rush to the defense of the rebel fleet at the Battle of Mako-Ta.]]
Later, X-wings defended the Alliance Fleet from an [[Battle of Mako-Ta|assault on the Mako-Ta Space Docks]], a major blow for the Rebellion. The attack destroyed more than half of the Rebel cruisers and 90 percent of its available starfighter forces.<ref name="Star Wars 52">[[Star Wars (2015) 52|''Star Wars'' (2015) 52]]</ref><ref name="Star Wars 55">[[Star Wars (2015) 55|''Star Wars'' (2015) 55]]</ref>

A number of X-wings accompanied the [[61st Mobile Infantry]] [[company]], known to most as "Twilight Company," on the [[Coyerti campaign]] in the [[Mid Rim Retreat]]. The campaign ended with the destruction of an Imperial [[biotoxin]] production facility and an Alliance victory.<ref name="Twilight Company">''[[Battlefront: Twilight Company]]''</ref>

=====From Hoth to Jakku=====
In [[3 ABY]], numerous X-wings served as fighter escorts for the Alliance's [[GR-75 medium transport]]s during the [[Battle of Hoth]]. The rearguard actions on the surface covering the evacuation proved costly to the Alliance, with many personnel killed. Additionally, the Alliance was forced to leave behind much of their heavy equipment, and the fleet, including its X-wings, scattered throughout the [[Outer Rim Territories]],<ref name="TESB" /> travelling to separate rendezvous points like [[Rendezvous Point Delta-Three]].<ref name="Star Wars 2020 1">[[Star Wars (2020) 1|''Star Wars'' (2020) 1]]</ref>

Luke Skywalker, however, traveled to the [[Dagobah system]] to seek out [[Yoda]], the former [[Grand Master]] of the [[Jedi Order]]. Due to [[Dagobah]]'s thick fog, Skywalker crashed his X-wing in a swamp.<ref name="TESB" /> With Skywalker away, [[Wedge Antilles]] was promoted to lead Rogue Squadron in his absence, which he rebranded to be "Red Squadron" due to the losses sustained on Hoth. The following day, Antilles led Red Squadron's X-wings against [[pirate]]s that threatened the security of<ref name="Rendezvous Point">{{StoryCite|story=Rendezvous Point (short story)|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}}</ref> Rendezvous Point Delta-Three.<ref name="Star Wars 2020 1" /> Meanwhile, Skywalker's starfighter sank further until it was almost fully submerged, at which point Skywalker attempted to recover it. While he had developed some skill with [[telekinesis]], his self-doubt led to his ultimate inability to lift his waterlogged X-wing from the bog, and only with Yoda's assistance was the starfighter moved to solid ground. When Skywalker left the system, he traveled to [[Bespin]], where he ended up abandoning his X-wing when circumstances compelled him to depart in the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]''.<ref name="TESB" />

Upon reaching Rendezvous Point Delta-Three, everyone aboard the ''Falcon'' found the [[Fourth Division]] [[Battle at Rendezvous Point Delta-Three|besieged]] by Imperial Commander [[Ellian Zahra]] and her [[Hunter Fleet]];<ref name="Star Wars 2020 1" /> having been appointed to find the Rebels,<ref name="Star Wars 2020 8">[[Star Wars (2020) 8|''Star Wars'' (2020) 8]]</ref> Zahra was able to track communications between the Fourth [[Division]] and [[Eighth Division]], which was [[Battle near Malastare|destroyed]] near [[Malastare]]. Zahra personally led the attack against the Fourth, trapping the X-wings and other craft between her fleet and a [[Star|sun]]. While one X-wing nearly escaped her forces, Zahra personally took control of a cannon to destroy it. However, the arrival of the ''Falcon'' eventually led to the Fourth Division successfully escaping to [[Backup Rendezvous Point Gamma-Nine]].<ref name="Star Wars 2020 1" /> Later, Skywalker reclaimed his personal X-wing during a [[mission to Cloud City]],<ref name="Star Wars 2020 4">[[Star Wars (2020) 4|''Star Wars'' (2020) 4]]</ref> and several of the Fourth Division's X-wings and [[A-wing]]s served together as [[Starlight Squadron]].<ref name="Star Wars 2020 10">[[Star Wars (2020) 10|''Star Wars'' (2020) 10]]</ref>

X-wings assisted Twilight Company in [[Operation Ringbreaker]], an attempt to divert Imperial forces from [[Kuat]] to make the planet more vulnerable to attack. The operation saw numerous engagements with X-wings in combat, including an [[attack on the dockyards of Najan-Rovi]]. The campaign scored some notable successes, but it ultimately ended with the [[Siege of Inyusu Tor]] and the failure to reach Kuat. Although the Alliance squad was stranded on [[Sullust]] and on the verge of defeat from the outset, an uprising of the [[Cobalt Laborers' Reformation Front]] liberated a part of the planet.<ref name="Twilight Company" />

In [[4 ABY]], [[Corona Squadron]] engaged Imperial TIEs in a [[dogfight in the Hudalla system]]. The small but drawn-out engagement resulted in each side losing a single starfighter, and it set the stage for the [[Battle of Endor]].<ref name="Lost Stars">''[[Lost Stars]]''</ref>

[[File:X-wings-and-DS2.png|thumb|left|300px|Two X-wings flee the second Death Star's explosion]]
By this time, Luke Skywalker had acquired another X-wing and flew it to [[Tatooine]] to lead the [[rescue of Han Solo]], who had been arrested by [[Boba Fett]] and encased in [[carbonite]] at [[Boba Fett's Palace|Jabba's Palace]]. Upon the successful completion of the rescue, Skywalker returned to Dagobah, fulfilling a promise to Yoda. After Yoda's death, Skywalker departed Dagobah for the final time, en route to Sullust to rejoin the Alliance fleet. On Skywalker's arrival, the entirety of the Alliance Fleet staged a large-scale assault on the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station]], an under-construction Imperial battle station with even more firepower than the original Death Star. Wedge Antilles and [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]], accompanied by a group of Fighter, led an attack run deep within the bowels of the station and fired ordnance at the reactor core, destroying the station.<ref name="ROTJ" />

Seventeen days after the Battle of Endor, X-wings took part in the [[Battle of Cawa City]], which expelled Imperial forces from [[Sterdic IV]].<ref name="Shattered Empire 2">[[Shattered Empire 2|''Shattered Empire'' 2]]</ref>

X-wings fought Imperial forces at the [[Attack on Fondor]] alongside [[A-wing starfighter|A-wings]] and [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft|U-wings]]. The battle ultimately ended with a Rebel defeat, and the Empire securing weather control [[satellite]]s for Operation Cinder.<ref name="Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]''</ref>

Luke Skywalker flew his X-wing to undertake a [[mission to Pillio]], where he encountered [[Del Meeko]].<ref name="Battlefront II" />

X-wings also engaged Imperial TIEs in the [[Battle of Theed]], which resulted in the destruction of a series of Imperial weather control satellites and the failure of [[Operation: Cinder]].<ref name="Shattered Empire 3">[[Shattered Empire 3|''Shattered Empire'' 3]]</ref>

By the end of the Battle of Naboo, the Alliance had reorganized itself into the [[New Republic]] and continued to operate the Alliance's Fighter.<ref name="Battlefront II" /> New Republic X-wings saw action at the [[Battle of Naalol]] and the [[Rebellion on Akiva]], both victories for the Republic.<ref name="Aftermath">[[Aftermath (novel)|''Aftermath'']]</ref>

In 5 ABY, the Empire continued to put up resistance against the New Republic's liberation of the galaxy. [[Inferno Squad (Resistance)|Inferno Squad]], a former Imperial special forces unit, flew X-wings against their former comrades in a [[skirmish on Takodana]]. Later, Inferno Squad would fly X-wings again in a [[mission to Chinook Station]].<ref name="Battlefront II" /> X-wings accompanied the [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter|A/SF-01 B-wing Fighter]] of [[Blade Squadron]] in the [[Defense of Kuat|Battle for Kuat Drive Yards]], which crippled the Empire's capability to produce starships and walkers.<ref name="Kuat">{{InsiderCite|168|Blade Squadron: Kuat}}</ref> The twelve X-wings of [[Phantom Squadron]] took part in the [[liberation of Kashyyyk]], which deprived the Empire of much of its slave labor.<ref name="Life Debt">''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]''</ref> Corona Squadron's X-wings fought Imperial forces during the [[Invasions of Naboo]].<ref name="Lost Stars" /> [[Shepherd Squadron]] operated X-wings in the [[Battle of Fondor Shipyards]]<ref name="Destroyer Down">''[[Star Wars Adventures: Destroyer Down]]''</ref>

The [[Galactic Concordance]] treaty was signed in the middle of the Battle of Jakku, which marked the final surrender of the Empire. The Imperial ships that hadn't been destroyed in the fighting began jumping into the [[Unknown Regions]], and went on to form the nucleus of the [[First Order Navy]].<ref name="TFA Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

====New Republic Era====
{{Quote|Are those X-wings?|[[Qin]]|<ref name="The Mandalorian">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 6: The Prisoner}}</ref>}}
In [[28 ABY]], the [[Amaxine warriors (New Republic Era)|Amaxine warriors]] operated numerous X-wings alongside Y-wings, B-wings, and Imperial TIEs. Although these Fighter were all destroyed in a [[mission to Sibensko]], the [[Amaxine warrior crisis]] resulted in the formation of the Resistance.<ref name="Bloodline" /> The [[B-class X-wing]] existed by the time of the New Republic Era and was represented in a model kit owned by a young [[Karr Nuq Sin]].<ref name="Force Collector">''[[Force Collector]]''</ref>

[[File:Resistance_X-wing_SWCT.png|thumb|250px|A T-70 X-wing starfighter]]
In [[33 ABY]], the New Republic T-85 X-wings of [[Rapier Squadron]] fought [[First Order]] TIEs over [[Suraz 4]]. The First Order hijacked the ''[[Yissira Zyde]]'' freighter during the [[Suraz engagement]], prompting [[Rapier Leader]] [[Poe Dameron]] to launch an unsanctioned mission to recover the ship. The resulting [[skirmish in OR-Kappa-2722]] led Dameron to trouble with the New Republic authorities, and Dameron defected to the Resistance shortly after.<ref name="Before the Awakening" />

During the [[hunt for Lor San Tekka]], the T-70 X-wings of [[Black Squadron (Resistance)|Black Squadron]] engaged First Order TIEs in a [[mission to Ovanis]].<ref name="Poe Dameron 1">[[Poe Dameron 1|''Poe Dameron'' 1]]</ref> The dogfight ended in a draw, although Black Squadron shot down several TIEs without suffering any casualties.<ref name="Poe Dameron 3">[[Poe Dameron 3|''Poe Dameron'' 3]]</ref>

Later on in [[34 ABY]], during the [[mission to Kaddak]], [[Commander]] Poe Dameron stowed his own personal T-70 X-wing, ''[[Black One]]'', in the cargo compartment of a freighter. After a series of complications required a quick evacuation from the planet, Dameron abandoned the freighter and left in ''Black One''.<ref name="Poe Dameron 10">[[Poe Dameron 10|''Poe Dameron'' 10]]</ref>

[[File:T85-TheRecruitPart1.jpg|thumb|left|250px|T-85 X-wing starfighter]]
Five Black Squadron Fighters, including four X-wings, engaged the forces of the First Order in a [[battle over a desert planet]]. The engagement led to the death of A-wing pilot [[L'ulo L'ampar]].<ref name="Poe Dameron 13">[[Poe Dameron 13|''Poe Dameron'' 13]]</ref>

Black Squadron operated T-70 X-wings in a [[mission to Spalex]].<ref name="Poe Dameron 17">[[Poe Dameron 17|''Poe Dameron'' 17]]</ref>

Black Squadron was also involved in a [[Mission to Cato Neimoidia (Resistance)|mission to Cato Neimoidia]], in which it faced off against Clone Wars–era [[Droid starfighter|droid fighter]].<ref name="Poe Dameron 21">[[Poe Dameron 21|''Poe Dameron'' 21]]</ref>

The young New Republic pilot later turned Resistance spy by Poe Dameron, [[Kazuda Xiono]], along with his [[Kazuda Xiono's team|squadron]], consisting of [[Hugh Sion]] and [[Mia Gabon]], engaged [[Major]] [[Elrik Vonreg's TIE Interceptor|Vonreg's Tie]] in deep space with their T-85 X-wings to [[Mission to rendezvous with the Resistance|provide]] Poe Dameron with critical intelligence about the First Order by the [[New Republic High Command|New Republic Command's]] orders.<ref name="The Recruit">{{Resistance|The Recruit}}</ref> Xiono and Dameron flew X-wings on missions together at least twice more in an [[Investigation of a G-class freighter]] and a [[Mission to Station Theta Black]].<ref name="Signal from Sector Six">{{Resistance|Signal from Sector Six}}</ref><ref name="Station Theta Black">{{Resistance|Station Theta Black (episode)}}</ref>

[[Zay Versio]] and [[Iden Versio]] both flew X-wings in a [[mission to Athulla]]. Later, [[Shriv Suurgav]] and Iden flew them to Vardos, where the two fought both First Order and Jinata Security forces in the [[Battle of Kestro City|battle of Kestro]].<ref name="Battlefront II" />

[[File:Black_One_BF2.png|thumb|right|185x185px|''Black One'' was Poe Dameron's personal T-70 X-wing.]]
At some point after [[Snoke]] drew [[Ben Solo]] to the dark side of the Force, renaming him Kylo Ren,<ref name="TLJ">{{Film|VIII}}</ref> he and the [[Knights of Ren]]<ref name="Updated and Expanded">''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]''</ref> killed all of Skywalker's students and burned the [[Jedi Temple of Luke Skywalker|Jedi temple]].<ref name="TLJ" /> Skywalker went into exile, and went in search of the [[First Jedi Temple]]. Before leaving, he gave half the map to his astromech droid, R2-D2, and the other half to [[Lor San Tekka]].<ref name="TFA">{{Film|VII}}</ref> After traveling to [[Ahch-To]], he landed his X-wing in a shallow inlet, leaving himself stranded on the [[Temple Island|island]], and cut himself from [[the Force]].<ref name="TLJ" />

Later, Dameron and [[BB-8]] flew a T-70 to [[Jakku]] in order to meet San Tekka in the village of [[Tuanul]]. San Tekka had in his possession the [[Map to Skywalker]], which was eagerly sought by both the First Order and the Resistance. The First Order also tracked down San Tekka and launched an [[attack on Tuanul]], killing him and all the villagers. Dameron attempted to flee in his X-wing, but the ship was damaged and subsequently destroyed.<ref name="TFA" />

====First Order-Resistance war====
{{Quote|That's one hell of a pilot!|Finn, on Poe Dameron's piloting skills|<ref name="TFA" />}}
[[File:X-wing_vs_TIE_fighter_on_Takodana.png|thumb|left|300px|Resistance X-wings mix it up with First Order TIEs in the skies of Takodana]]
Within hours, the First Order's learned that the droid had escaped to [[Takodana Castle]], and initiated the [[Battle of Takodana]] in an attempt to recover BB-8 and the map. [[Han Solo]], [[Chewbacca]], and Finn were captured, but the X-wings of the [[Resistance Starfighter Corps|Starfighter Corps]] intervened and forced the First Order's ground forces to retreat, allowing the trio to escape.<ref name="TFA" />

Upon learning that the First Order planned to destroy the [[Resistance base]] in the [[Ileenium system]], the Resistance deployed a force of T-70 X-wings in a desperate [[Battle of Starkiller Base]]. Despite the loss of all but seven X-wings in the offensive, the Resistance managed to destroy the base's [[thermal oscillator]], resulting in the destruction of the base.<ref name="TFA" />

The First Order soon retaliated, however, with another attack on the Resistance's main base. Dameron led a force of X-wings, A-wings, and [[MG-100 StarFortress SF-17 heavy bomber|MG-100 StarFortress SF-17]] bombers into battle to cover the [[Battle of D'Qar|evacuation of D'Qar]]. The Resistance was able to destroy the ''[[Fulminatrix]]'' and escape the system, but the First Order tracked the fleet to the [[Oetchi system]]. There, Kylo Ren and his wingmen destroyed the entire Resistance Starfighter Corps while their craft were still parked in the [[Raddus (MC85 Star Cruiser)|''Raddus'']]{{'s}} hangar.<ref name="TLJ" />

==Behind the scenes==
The X-wing series of fighter first appeared in {{Film|IV}}, during the climactic Battle of Yavin. These ships quickly became iconic of the original film, the [[original trilogy]], and the ''[[Star Wars]]'' franchise as a whole. X-wings reappeared in the other two films of the original trilogy, {{Film|V}} and {{Film|VI}}. Many [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] products also featured the X-wings and their crewmembers, including [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']], ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance]]'', ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Miniatures Game]]'', and ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron]]''. [[Lucasfilm]] also created numerous ships that served as [[in-universe]] predecessors and successors of the X-wing, including the [[Z-95 Headhunter/Legends|Z-95 Headhunter]] starfighter, [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter/Legends|ARC-170 starfighter]], and [[X-83 TwinTail starfighter]].

On [[April 25]], [[2014]], Lucasfilm announced that the Expanded Universe would be discontinued and rebranded as "Legends" in anticipation of the upcoming {{Film|VII}}. All existing Expanded Universe material was declared non-[[canon]], and the only previously published works that would still be canon were the original trilogy, prequel trilogy, the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]] and TV series, and Part I of [[Blade Squadron (short story)|''Blade Squadron'']]. All products published on or after that date, with the exception of the continuation of a few Legends stories, would be part of a new, unified canonicity system in which all works were declared either canon or non-canon from the outset. Legends characters, organizations, titles, creatures, sentient species, droid models, vehicles, vessels, events, weapons, and locations would still be available for authors of new canon material with the approval of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]].

After the announcement, Lucasfilm began publishing new canon material that introduced new X-wing models, including the T-70 and T-85 X-wing fighters. An X-wing model that was formerly unique to Legends, the T-65C-A2 X-wing starfighter, was re-canonized by the release of ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]''.
